quandoUsar: When order matters more than values: who led, who overtook whom, and in which period.
Rankings by period with few items, such as regions by month or teams by round, with each series' name at the end of its line.
Switch the ranking measure while keeping the items: series with the same `key` slide to the new positions.
quandoEvitar: Use `line-chart` when the distance between values matters: here only the position appears in the drawing.
Use `slope-chart` to compare exactly two moments.
Use `sortable-data-table` for the ranking of a single period with several columns.

teclado.acao: Moves focus to the chart area and brings forward the series that is first in the last period.
Moves to the series one position above or below in the current period.
Moves to the previous or next period, keeping the series.
Moves to the first or last period.
Releases the series: all return to the same weight.

acessibilidade: The reading area is a vertical `role="slider"` whose `aria-valuetext` states the series, period, position, value, and the change since the previous period.
A hidden table carries the position and value of each series in each period; `label` is required and names the figure.
Ordinals and tooltip phrases (“1st of 6”, “Up 2 from Oct”) are generated in English in the code and have no translation prop.
movimento: On first appearance each line draws from the first to the last period, one series after another, and the points appear following the stroke.

When the data changes, lines, points, and names slide with a no-overshoot spring to the new positions; the focused series gets a thicker stroke and a ring with the position in each period, and the others fade.
With “reduce motion”, everything appears and swaps immediately, and the tooltip jumps instead of sliding.
responsivo: The height is `rowHeight` (40 px) times the number of series and the width is the container's; the names column takes up to 36% and truncates with an ellipsis.
Period labels do not thin out when space runs short: with many periods on a narrow screen they overlap, so use short labels.
notasIA: Each series is `{ key, label, values, color? }`, with one value per item in `periods` in the same order; positions are computed from the values, and `order="asc"` puts the smallest first (times, costs).
Focused series: controlled with `activeKey` and `onActiveChange` (`null` for none), or uncontrolled with `defaultActiveKey`.
The first four series use `--series-1` to `--series-4` and the following ones, three neutral tones that repeat from the eighth: pass `color` if there are more.
